title: Resume VCF Installer task paging after access-token refresh
prompt:
Implement the standard-library-only Java client in the single file `VcfInstallerClient.java`. Do not add dependencies or edit any other file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection derived directly from `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable VCF 9.1 release-readiness commit `3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26`. `docs/official_sources.json` records the exact specification path, repository commit SHA, and a separate specification source record for every operationId. No rendered documentation page is a contract source. Use exactly the specification operationIds `getTasks` and `refreshAccessToken`; do not call another route.

Preserve the supplied public API and nested types: `new VcfInstallerClient(String baseUrl, String accessToken, String refreshTokenId)`, `List<Task> listAllTasks(TaskQuery query)`, `TaskQuery`, `Task`, `VcfApiException`, `ProtocolException`, and `TransportException`. The service root must be an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL with a host and no userinfo, non-root path, query, or fragment. Reject a blank or header-unsafe access token, a blank refresh-token ID, a null query, and a page size outside 1 through the specification maximum of 100 before sending anything. Never expose either token, response bodies, or an underlying transport-error string in an exception message.

Retrieve the entire zero-based `getTasks` collection. The first request sends `pageSize` but omits `pageNumber`; later requests send the next `pageNumber` and the same `pageSize`. Preserve accepted earlier pages in memory. If a `getTasks` attempt returns exact HTTP 401, call `refreshAccessToken` once for that invocation and retry the same page with the returned access token. Do not restart at page zero, discard accepted tasks, skip the interrupted page, or change its query. All later pages use the refreshed access token. A second 401 is final and must not cause another refresh. Any refresh failure aborts without returning partial results. Treat exact HTTP 200 as success for both named operations. Other `getTasks` statuses, except the one refresh-triggering 401, and every non-200 refresh status throw `VcfApiException` with the relevant operationId and actual status.

`TaskQuery`'s nullable components are the specification's optional `getTasks` filters. Omit every null component completely: `limit`, `taskStatus`, `taskType`, `resourceId`, `resourceType`, `completedAfter`, `orderDirection`, `orderBy`, `taskName`, and `doLiveRefresh`. Never serialize an unset option as an empty value, zero, false, `null`, or a placeholder. Preserve non-null values exactly, including empty strings, numeric zero, and explicit false. Add client-managed `pageSize` and, after the first page, `pageNumber`; do not invent any other query member. Encode string values as UTF-8 RFC 3986 query components. Emit parameters in `TaskQuery` declaration order, followed by `pageSize`, then `pageNumber` when present. Never emit a bare `?`.

Require JSON media type on every successful response. `refreshAccessToken` is `PATCH /v1/tokens/access-token/refresh`; its request body is the refresh-token ID encoded as one JSON string, not an object, with exact JSON escaping. It has exactly one `Accept: application/json` and one `Content-Type: application/json`, a fixed UTF-8 content length, no transfer encoding, no query, and no `Authorization` header carrying the expired token. Its success body must be a nonblank, header-safe JSON string. `getTasks` is a bodyless `GET /v1/tasks`. Each attempt has exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <currentAccessToken>` and one `Accept: application/json`, no `Content-Type`, body, transfer encoding, or positive content length.

Decode each `PageOfTask` and validate it before adding that page: `elements` must be a non-null array; `pageMetadata` must be an object whose `pageNumber`, `pageSize`, `totalElements`, and `totalPages` are non-boolean integers; page numbers must match the requested zero-based page; totals must remain stable; page counts must agree with the requested page size; metadata page size must equal the current element count and not exceed the request; non-final pages must be full; the final accumulated count must equal `totalElements`; and task IDs must not repeat. Every Task must have nonblank specification-required `id`, `name`, `status`, and `creationTimestamp`. Its optional `type` must remain null when absent and must be a string when present. Return a fresh unmodifiable list only after the full collection succeeds; every failure returns no partial list.

Run `java TestMain.java`. The protected verifier starts the shipped contract-pinned mock on ephemeral `127.0.0.1` ports and reads its synchronized request log. In the main scenario page zero succeeds with the initial token, page one reports token expiry, refresh returns a new access token, page one is retried exactly, and page two completes. The verifier asserts the exact raw targets, headers, body bytes, content lengths, no restart or lost page, single refresh, optional-value omission versus explicit empty/zero/false, query escaping, protocol checks, and validation before wire. The mock loads and serves only the two operations named by `docs/contract.json`. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.
scenario: The initial access token expires on page one of getTasks; refreshAccessToken supplies a replacement and the client retries that page without repeating or losing page zero.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves the precise five-attempt wire sequence and complete omission of every unset optional getTasks query parameter.
